headline: Kalaburagi faces high malnutrition, poverty, and child marriage, with government interventions showing limited local impact
summary: Kalaburagi is identified as one of Karnataka's poorest districts with significant malnutrition concerns. The 2022 Human Development Report flagged Kalaburagi for both poverty and nutrition issues, recommending agricultural interventions to lift at least 20% of the population from poverty. In 2021, children in Kalaburagi, Raichur and Yadgir were specifically identified as suffering from malnutrition, prompting the Chief Minister to plan a special programme targeting children's health and education. Kalaburagi also faces high teenage pregnancy rates and child marriage, with 1648 teenage pregnancies reported in one year. District authorities have directed strict measures against child labour and child marriage.

reasons.detail: Kalaburagi flagged as one of Karnataka's poorest districts with poverty rates of 18.36 percent, limiting access to adequate nutrition and health services.
High teenage pregnancy rates (1648 cases in one year) and child marriage prevalence indicate poor maternal health conditions affecting child outcomes.
Low farm productivity identified; government report recommends agricultural interventions to improve incomes and reduce poverty-driven malnutrition.
Traditional mindsets hinder children's education; child marriage prevalent with 80 girls' marriages prevented in recent drives.

modelFactorWhy.why: Pages document poor educational outcomes and traditional mindsets preventing children's education in Kalaburagi. Child marriage remains prevalent, with 80 marriages prevented. However, no direct data on preschool enrollment for ages 3-6.
modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Early schooling supports cognitive development and may improve health knowledge and nutrition practices in families.

Kalaburagi and Yadgir districts have consistently performed poorly in school education

modelFactorWhy.factor: Mothers who took iron-folic acid for 180+ days in pregnancy
modelFactorWhy.why: High teenage pregnancy rates (1648 cases) indicate poor maternal health preparation. Study from Kalaburagi documents iron deficiency anemia as predominant during pregnancy. However, no specific data on 180+ day iron-folic acid compliance.
modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Iron-folic acid prevents maternal anemia, reduces preterm births and intrauterine growth restriction, improving birth outcomes.

proof.claim: Study from Kalaburagi states iron deficiency anemia is predominant during pregnancy with increased requirement of iron and folic acid

modelFactorWhy.factor: Household members covered by health insurance
modelFactorWhy.why: No pages contain information about health insurance coverage among households in Kalaburagi district. Poverty data suggests economic barriers to healthcare but insurance coverage is not documented.
modelFactorWhy.mechanism: Health insurance enables access to preventive and curative healthcare services, reducing out-of-pocket costs for treatment.
